name: Crispy lamb over yogurt with kabocha, pomegranate, and dates
time: 35 minutes, or 15 if the squash is already roasted
yield: Dinner tonight and a second plate
intro: Lamb browned until it crackles, spooned hot over cold salted yogurt, with sweet roasted squash, dates, and pomegranate. Rich, sour, sweet, and crisp in every forkful.
needs: Rice or toasted sourdough, to serve

steps.text: Heat the oven. Toss the kabocha with oil and salt and roast until the edges are dark and a knife slides through.
Stir a big pinch of salt and a squeeze of lemon into the yogurt. Spread half of it on a plate.
Put the lamb in a dry skillet over medium-high, press it flat, and don't touch it until it crusts underneath.
Break it up and keep cooking until it's browned all over and crackling at the edges.
Add the garlic, a pinch of chile flakes, and salt for the last minute, and stir the dates in to warm them.
Squash on the yogurt, lamb over it, pomegranate and arugula on top, lemon squeezed over everything.

how_it_works: Rich meat wants something sour and something sweet against it. Here the yogurt and pomegranate cut the fat, and the dates and squash round it out. Browning the lamb hard — flat in the pan, left alone — turns its fat into crisp edges, which is most of the flavor.
swaps: No lamb? Ground beef works the same way, or leftover pork tenderloin, sliced and warmed.
No roasted squash? Serve it over rice and let the yogurt carry it.
leftovers: Half the lamb keeps four days. Tomorrow it's toast for dinner, or the filling for a baked sweet potato.
